name: Steroid back acne management

lead: Steroid back acne is acne on the back and shoulders that people attribute to anabolic steroid or testosterone use. People who train for physique want to keep that area clear so the back and shoulders look clean as well as built.

Androgen levels rise, sebum output increases, and breakouts appear on the oil-rich skin of the back. Wikipedia describes acne as a recognised effect of anabolic-androgenic steroids and testosterone replacement. Available reference material covers general acne and androgens; no trial dedicated to back acne from performance-enhancing steroids was found.

paras: People generally lean on standard acne care for the back: regular washing after training, clean fabrics against the skin, and over-the-counter or prescribed acne products. Forum discussion treats it as an ongoing side effect to manage rather than a one-time fix, and persistent cases are usually taken to a clinician.
Anabolic steroids carry broader legal and health risks beyond skin. Severe or scarring acne is usually managed by clinicians, and prescription acne drugs have their own side effects.

angle.text: The goal is a clear back and shoulders while building a physique. Rising androgen levels increase sebum output, and back and shoulder acne appears; acne is a recognised effect of anabolic steroids and testosterone. Management advice draws mostly on general acne information.

lead: Steroid back acne, often shortened to bacne in training forums, is acne on the back, shoulders and chest that people connect with anabolic-androgenic steroid or testosterone use. For people building a physique, the skin of the upper body matters as much as the muscle under it, so managing breakouts there is a recurring topic in lifting and looksmaxxing communities [1][2].

Dermatology literature uses the term steroid acne for acne caused by corticosteroids or anabolic-androgenic steroids, and a 1989 review in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology described a sequence of follicular changes leading to microcomedones and then inflamed papules and pustules [3][4]. Wikipedia lists testosterone and glucocorticoids among medications that can worsen acne, and calls the form caused by anabolic-androgenic steroids steroid acne [1].

Communities discuss the topic as a skin-clarity question: what causes it, how it differs from other back conditions, and when to see a dermatologist. No published trial has tested treatments specifically for back acne in anabolic steroid users; clinicians draw on general acne care [1].
infobox: Topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, antibiotics, isotretinoin (clinician-directed) [1]

paras: Androgens such as testosterone, DHT and DHEA are linked to acne because they increase sebum production, and acne does not develop in people with complete androgen insensitivity syndrome [1]. Acne favours skin with many oil glands, including the face, upper chest and back [1]. Wikipedia lists medications that can worsen existing acne, including lithium, glucocorticoids and testosterone, and uses steroid acne for the form caused by anabolic-androgenic steroids [1].

sections.h: Steroid acne in the medical literature
paras: A 1989 review in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology said steroid acne had become more common with organ transplantation and cancer treatment regimens, and described a sequence of infundibular spongiosis, hyperkeratosis, microcomedo formation and rupture leading to papules and papulopustules [3]. A 2003 dermatology nursing article and a 2025 British Journal of Dermatology report on steroid acne fluorescing under ultraviolet light also address the condition [5][6]. Reviews of topical clobetasol list steroid acne among the effects of prolonged use of superpotent topical glucocorticoids [7].
A 1999 Japanese review found Malassezia in follicular contents of both steroid acne and acne vulgaris, which dermatologists note when distinguishing acne-like eruptions from fungal folliculitis [8].

Wikipedia lists first-line treatments for acne vulgaris as topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide and topical or oral antibiotics, with isotretinoin reserved by clinicians for severe cases, and notes azelaic acid and salicylic acid as other topical options [1]. Diagnosis includes a medication review, since drugs can contribute [1]. Forum participants on T Nation commonly recommend a visit to a dermatologist when breakouts are severe, and describe androgen-driven oil production as the cause [9].

No studies found examining management of back acne specifically in anabolic steroid users. Related literature covers steroid acne in clinical case descriptions and reviews [3][5][6], and a 1983 randomized trial found that topical betamethasone valerate on the face caused no significant change in skin flora compared with placebo [10].

lore.intro: On T Nation, bacne appears in threads on steroid use, cruising doses and appearance, with members disagreeing about what it indicates and how to handle it [9][2][11].
